brief: Explain to curious adults why most coasts see two high tides a day. The Moon's gravity pulls the ocean into a bulge on the side facing it, and a second bulge forms on the far side; as the Earth turns, a coastline passes through both. Mention that the Sun adds to the effect, making larger tides when Sun and Moon line up. Keep it accurate and unhurried; no myths, no exaggeration.
